answer: Naive design counts signatures; better design decays them. Each trust edge loses weight every epoch it goes unrefreshed, and an identity unlocks vouching only after continuous uptime, so a burst of new accounts cannot vote for each other on day one. Quorum must span unrelated subnetworks, meaning a basalt cluster inside one AS never reaches threshold. Faking a glacier of identities means paying uptime for each and finding neighbours outside your own oasis.
